change.title: pr-8
change.description: FIX: proper handling of group memberships
change.author: Régis Hanol

findings.title: Public group members page now shows only the first 50 members, with no pager
findings.body: `members` now defaults to `limit = 50` (groups_controller.rb:22). The only in-repo caller of the public endpoint is the members route, which calls `findMembers` once with the group's default `limit: 50` (discourse/models/group.js:10, 25-29; discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:11). `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` renders that list with no pager. The group tab still shows the full total `({{counts.members}})` (discourse/templates/group.hbs:11). Before this change, non-automatic groups returned every member and automatic groups returned up to 200. So a group with more than 50 members now shows a partial list with no indication and no way to reach the rest. Fix: add previous/next controls to the public members page (the admin page already has them), or keep an unpaginated request for this caller. Also, the pagination spec at spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb:72 is still `pending` and parses the body as a bare array (line 78), which the new `{members, meta}` shape would break; it needs updating when it is enabled.

findings.title: totalPages is one too high when the member count is an exact multiple of the page size
findings.body: `totalPages` computes `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` (line 13). With 50 members and limit 50 it gives 2 pages, but there is only one. Clicking next from page 1 sets offset to 50 (`next`, lines 33-35), the server returns an empty list, and the pager shows "2/2" over an empty table. The same happens at 100, 150, and so on. A second case: after removing the only member on the last page, `removeMember` calls `findMembers` (discourse/models/group.js:47), and the clamp at group.js:23 uses the stale `user_count` (still the old total), so the reload requests the old offset and shows an empty page with no automatic step back. Fix: use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` for totalPages, and after a reload clamp offset to the last valid page.

findings.title: remove_member bypasses Group#remove, so the cached user_count is not decremented
findings.body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` on a has_many :through runs a bulk delete of the join rows without callbacks (Rails 4.1.8, Gemfile.lock:307). The counter cache lives on `GroupUser belongs_to :group, counter_cache: "user_count"` (app/models/group_user.rb:2), so it is never decremented. The removed incremental path called `group.remove(user)` (the deleted `update_patch` loop), which is `group_users.where(user: user).each(&:destroy)` (app/models/group.rb:276-278) and does run the callback. The stored `groups.user_count` therefore drifts upward on every removal. That value feeds the admin groups list (BasicGroupSerializer, which exposes user_count). The admin page corrects itself on reload because `findMembers` takes `meta.total` from a live count. Fix: use `group.remove(User.find(user_id))` or destroy the GroupUser row directly. Note that admin/users_controller.rb:128 (`remove_group`) uses the same `users.delete` pattern; that is outside this part and pre-existing. Confidence is medium because the Rails 4.1.8 source is not in the repository and the claim rests on that behavior.

findings.title: Adding a user who is already a member fails with a unique-index error, and the UI reports nothing
findings.body: `add_members` calls `group.add(user)` for each name (lines 71-75). `Group#add` is `users.push(user)` (app/models/group.rb:272-274) with no existence check. `group_users` has a unique index on (group_id, user_id) (app/models/group_user.rb:18), so re-adding an existing member raises a database error and the request returns a 500. Names processed before the failing one are already inserted, since there is no transaction. On the client, `addMembers` has no failure handler (discourse/models/group.js:51-60; admin-group.js.es6:61-65), and the input is never cleared (the TODO at admin-group.js.es6:62). So a second click on "Add" resubmits the same names and fails silently, and the list is not refreshed. Fix: skip users who are already members (or rescue the error per user), clear the input on success, and show the error on failure. Confidence is medium because the push-without-dedupe behavior of has_many :through is taken from Rails and not read here.

findings.title: create ignores alias_level, so the alias chosen for a new group is silently dropped
findings.body: The new-group form shows the alias combo box (admin/templates/group.hbs:41-44). `save` calls `group.create()` for new groups (admin-group.js.es6:77). `create` sends `alias_level` through `asJSON` (discourse/models/group.js:65, 70-75). The controller reads only `name` and `visible` (admin/groups_controller.rb:24-25) and never sets alias_level, so the group is saved with the default (0) regardless of what the user picked. The base `create` also ignored alias_level, so this predates the PR, but this PR rewrote `create` and kept the gap. Fix: set `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?` before `save`, as `update` does at line 37.

findings.title: Member-load failures are no longer surfaced
findings.body: `setupController` calls `model.findMembers()` and neither returns nor handles its promise (line 13). The previous `afterModel` returned the promise, so a failed load reached the route's error handling. Now a failed request leaves an empty or stale member list with no message. The same applies to the public members route (discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:11). Fix: either return the promise from a hook as before, or attach a failure handler that shows an error.

findings.title: Does `automatic` resolve inside the member item view?
findings.body: The item view's context is the member, not the group (group.hbs:21 uses `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`). If `{{#unless automatic}}` does not look up the group's `automatic` in this context, the remove link is shown for automatic groups. Clicking it gets a 422 (admin/groups_controller.rb:88) and nothing is displayed, because `removeMember` has no failure handler (admin-group.js.es6:56-57; discourse/models/group.js:40-49). Could you confirm whether the link is hidden on automatic groups in the browser? If not, pass `automatic` into the item view explicitly.

findings.title: Pressing Enter in the name field fires the "Add" button, not Save
findings.body: The form has no submit handler. The buttons have no `type`, so they are submit buttons. Implicit submission (Enter in a text field) clicks the form's first submit button in tree order. For an existing non-automatic group that is the "Add" button at line 29, not Save at line 47. The result is that Enter in the name field runs `addMembers` and never saves the name. Fix: set `type="button"` on the non-submit buttons, or bind the form submit to `save`.

findings.title: Negative or unbounded limit/offset are not validated
findings.body: `limit` and `offset` come straight from params (lines 22-23). A negative `offset` or `limit` produces a negative OFFSET or LIMIT in the SQL, which PostgreSQL rejects with an error, so the request returns a 500. There is also no upper bound on `limit`, so one request can return the whole membership. Fix: clamp `offset` to at least 0 and `limit` to a range such as 1..N.

findings.title: The remove_member test sends PUT, but the route is DELETE; coverage gaps remain
findings.body: `remove_member` is routed as DELETE (config/routes.rb:49), but the test at line 115 sends `xhr :put`. Controller specs do not check the verb, so the test passes, but it does not exercise the route's real verb. The spec file also has no coverage for: updating the name of a non-automatic group or its alias_level (`.update` only tests an automatic group, lines 49-60); adding a user who is already a member (the case in the finding above); or a removal that should change `user_count` (the case in the finding above). Fix: use `:delete` at line 115 and add the missing cases.

findings.title: The `input#group-users` selector no longer matches anything
findings.body: The group user-selector's id changed from `group-users` to `user-selector` (admin/templates/group.hbs:28). The 600px rule at lines 1054-1060 (`.row.groups input#group-users`) is dead, so the selector now falls back to the 500px text-input rule at line 1055. Fix: change the selector to `#user-selector` or remove the rule.

findings.title: Stray closing `` inside the members table
findings.body: Line 19 closes a `div` that was never opened, inside the `<table>`. This is pre-existing, but the file is in this PR (line 6 changed). Fix: remove the tag.

findings.title: Labels `for="name"` and `for="alias"` do not point at the controls
findings.body: `text-field` and `combo-box` take the `name` attribute, not `id`, so the labels at lines 7 and 42 are not associated with their inputs. The user-selector label at line 27 does match its `id`. Fix: give those controls matching `id`s, or drop the `for` attributes.

contracts.action: Admin group page: load and page through members (pager next/previous, member count)
contracts.equivalent_path: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:8-12 (loads members via findMembers); base admin route afterModel loaded the full list
contracts.before_after: Before: the admin route's afterModel loaded all members (no paging). Now: setupController calls findMembers, which requests one page (limit 50, offset clamped to user_count) and sets user_count, offset, limit and members from meta. next/previous change offset and reload.
contracts.visible_effect: Pager shows currentPage/totalPages and the header shows (user_count). totalPages is wrong when user_count is an exact multiple of the limit, which yields an empty last page.
contracts.failure_mode: A failed findMembers is unhandled, so the list stays empty or stale with no message. The pager state is not reset after total changes, so an empty page can be shown.

contracts.action: Admin group page: add members ("Add" button, incremental PUT of usernames)
contracts.equivalent_path: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:65-82 (add_members) and app/models/group.rb:272-274 (add); the removed base update_put set the whole membership from usernames
contracts.before_after: Before: membership was replaced by the usernames string sent with the group PUT. Now: each name is added with Group#add; the list reloads on success; the input is not cleared.
contracts.visible_effect: The list reloads and the count updates after a successful add. Repeating the add with the same names is not handled.
contracts.failure_mode: A name already in the group raises a unique-index error (500). Earlier names in the same request stay added. There is no error handler, so nothing is shown and the list is not refreshed.

contracts.action: Admin group page: remove a member (row link, bootbox confirm, DELETE)
contracts.equivalent_path: app/models/group.rb:276-278 (Group#remove, which runs GroupUser destroy callbacks); the removed incremental delete in update_patch used it. Also app/controllers/admin/users_controller.rb:128 uses the same users.delete pattern.
contracts.before_after: Before: removal ran Group#remove (destroy per join row, so the counter cache fired). Now: group.users.delete(user_id) (a bulk delete of join rows), followed by findMembers.
contracts.visible_effect: The member list reloads. The stored user_count is not decremented, so the admin groups list shows a stale count.
contracts.failure_mode: No failure handler on removeMember. A 422 for an automatic group or a 404 for a non-member is silent. Whether the remove link is hidden on automatic groups depends on the open question on group_member.hbs.
contracts.open_question: Does Rails 4.1.8 has_many :through delete (group.users.delete) remove join rows with delete_all, so GroupUser's counter_cache is not decremented? If so the removal path needs group.remove. Also: does {{#unless automatic}} in group_member.hbs resolve against the group?

contracts.action: Public group members page (tab) loads the member list
contracts.before_after: Before: the route loaded all members for normal groups and up to 200 for automatic groups. Now: findMembers requests the first page of 50 and the template has no pager.
contracts.visible_effect: Only the first 50 members are listed, while the tab count shows the full total.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent truncation for groups over 50 members. No way to reach the rest from the UI.

contracts.action: Admin group page: save an existing group (PUT /admin/groups/:id)
contracts.before_after: Before: the PUT also carried usernames, which replaced membership. Now: the PUT sends name, alias_level and visible only; update ignores name for automatic groups.
contracts.visible_effect: Name, alias and visibility save. Membership is no longer changed by Save.
contracts.failure_mode: update sets visible to false when the param is absent (groups_controller.rb:38, admin_groups_controller.rb:38). The UI always sends visible, so no impact in-app.

contracts.action: Admin group page: create a new group (POST /admin/groups)
contracts.before_after: Before: create read name, usernames and visible. Now: create reads name and visible only, and the new form also shows alias_level.
contracts.visible_effect: The chosen alias level is not stored; the group is created with the default.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent loss of the alias_level the user chose.

contracts.action: Admin group route: revisit a group (the shared model keeps offset and members across visits)
contracts.equivalent_path: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:10-11,20-38 (offset and members stored on the group model)
contracts.before_after: Before: afterModel reloaded members from the start each time. Now: setupController calls findMembers with the stored offset, so a revisit reopens the page last viewed.
contracts.visible_effect: Returning to a group opens the last page viewed, not the first. The pager and list stay consistent with each other.
contracts.failure_mode: None beyond the page-state choice. Members from a previous visit show until the request returns.

contracts.equivalent_path: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/resolver (customResolve) with other admin views using templateName 'admin/templates/...' (e.g. admin/views/admin_api_view.js)
contracts.before_after: Before: the list rendered inline in the group template. Now: each item is a view resolved as view:group-member.
contracts.visible_effect: Each member row renders via admin/templates/group_member.
contracts.failure_mode: None in the resolver path: customResolve finds the module ending in views/group-member, and the template key matches group_member.hbs.

contracts.action: Admin group form: pressing Enter in the name field
contracts.equivalent_path: none in repo (form submission in other admin form templates)
contracts.before_after: Before: the form had no submit button in the group template. Now: the "Add" and "Save" buttons have no type, so the browser treats them as submit buttons.
contracts.visible_effect: Enter in the name field clicks the first submit button (Add) rather than saving the group.
contracts.failure_mode: The name is not saved on Enter; the user sees no change.
contracts.open_question: Confirm in a browser that Enter in the name field fires the Add button's action (implicit submission to the first submit button), and that the Save button is not reached.

contracts.action: Public members endpoint with limit/offset params
contracts.equivalent_path: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19-36 before the PR (unpaginated for normal groups; limit 200 default for automatic groups)
contracts.before_after: Before: no caller-supplied limit/offset for normal groups. Now: limit defaults to 50, offset defaults to 0, and both are passed straight to the query.
contracts.visible_effect: Valid requests return a page and meta.
contracts.failure_mode: A negative offset or limit leads to a database error (500). No upper bound on limit.

contracts.action: Admin routes for member add and remove
contracts.equivalent_path: config/routes.rb:45-47 (refresh_automatic_groups in the same resources block, under the same AdminConstraint)
contracts.before_after: Before: the nested get "users" route existed with no matching action. Now: delete and put on members are nested under :group_id.
contracts.visible_effect: DELETE/PUT /admin/groups/:group_id/members reach groups#remove_member and groups#add_members. The routes resolve as the controller reads them (params.require(:group_id)).
contracts.failure_mode: None found: AdminConstraint applies to the whole resources block.

contracts.action: Admin group and badge form styles (.groups, .badges .form-horizontal)
contracts.before_after: Before: the label, input and checkbox rules sat under a section.details block in the stylesheet. Now: they sit under .groups, .badges. The .badges rules keep the same selectors and values.
contracts.visible_effect: The groups page gets the same form styles as badges. The 600px user-selector width no longer applies (dead selector at line 1058).
contracts.failure_mode: No other admin template uses .form-horizontal inside section.details (checked: only group.hbs, badges-show.hbs, site_settings_category.hbs use it), so the removal affects no other page.

summary: I reviewed all 16 files in this part and found no blockers. Four fixes are the most important: (1) the public members page now shows only the first 50 members with no pager; (2) totalPages is one too high when the member count is an exact multiple of the page size, which shows an empty last page; (3) remove_member uses group.users.delete, which skips the user_count counter cache that Group#remove maintains; (4) adding an existing member raises a unique-index error, and the UI shows nothing. Also a fix: create drops the chosen alias_level. Consider-level items cover failure handling, Enter-key submission, negative limit/offset (500), a spec using the wrong verb, and a dead stylesheet selector. Two findings depend on Rails/Ember behaviour I could not check in the repo: the counter-cache drift (Rails 4.1.8 source) and the automatic check inside the member item view (raised as a question).
